title: Zero-trust sensitive-data POC hosting options analysis
content:
Purpose:
This note compares hosted, dedicated, and private hosting options for a regulated-customer POC that requires a zero-trust posture for sensitive data (PII, payment tokens, financial records). Goal is to produce an actionable recommendation and a short POC plan that validates security controls, latency/cost tradeoffs, and operational runbooks.

Context and assumptions:
- Customer: mid-market payments platform processing user-submitted statements and KYC artifacts.
- Data sensitivity: tokenized account identifiers and scanned ID docs considered high-sensitivity; other metadata considered low-sensitivity.
- Traffic profile for POC: 30 TPS peak, 10k tokens/request average 350 tokens per call, 60% generation, 40% embeddings/reranking.
- Compliance targets: SOC2 + regional data residency (EU), optional FIPS/KMS requirement for later production.
- Timeline: 6-8 week POC window.
- Budget constraint: POC budget target ~USD 8k-15k for infra credits, not including engineering time.

Evaluation criteria (decision drivers):
1) Data isolation and control (encryption keys, HSM/KMS access, audit logs)
2) Network isolation and egress control (VPC peering, private link, firewall rules)
3) Latency and performance (p95 TL < 220ms for short prompts, end-to-end 1–2s for large generation)
4) Operational complexity and time-to-result (onboard time, infra setup, SRE effort)
5) Predictable cost and ability to reserve capacity
6) Rollback and graceful degradation strategies
7) Compliance artifacts and evidence for customer audit

Option comparison (summary):
- Hosted (Redwood API):
  - Data controls: Customer can restrict models and request-level redaction; Redwood logs and tenant isolation are standard but customer does not control KMS/HSM by default. Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) available only on enterprise plan or Private offering.
  - Network: TLS only; no VPC peering in standard hosted account. Private endpoints via Dedicated/Private required.
  - Latency: Lowest onboarding latency. Multi-region endpoints available. Per-request latency depends on multi-tenant performance; good for iterative POC.
  - Ops: Minimal setup (API keys, prompt templates, sample dataset).
  - Cost: Pay-as-you-go; good for exploratory work.
  - Fit: Best when customer accepts provider-managed KMS/logging and prefers speed over maximal control.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity pool):
  - Data controls: Isolated GPU pool and tenant-level network controls; options for customer VPC peering and long-term node reservations. BYOK possible with contractual add-on; logs can be routed to customer log sink.
  - Network: Private link / VPC peering, IP allowlists, ability to restrict egress.
  - Latency: More predictable p95; capacity guarantees reduce throttling/fallbacks.
  - Ops: Moderate setup time (capacity reservation, routing, test harness). SRE involvement heavier than hosted.
  - Cost: Upfront commit or monthly charges; better when throughput predictable.
  - Fit: Good middle ground when customer needs stronger isolation but not full private control of control plane.

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - Data controls: Full customer control of KMS/HSM, audit logs, and physical network boundaries. No shared control plane; can be air-gapped.
  - Network: VPC-only, direct peering to customer infra, strict egress rules enforced by customer network.
  - Latency: Can be lowest for local on-prem resources; dependent on customer's infra.
  - Ops: Highest onboarding burden and longest lead time (network & security reviews, install windows). Requires customer infra and SRE/infra team.
  - Cost: Licensing/installation fees plus ops. Best when compliance requires complete control.
  - Fit: Required when regulation demands customer-held keys or air-gapped processing.

Security-focused tradeoffs and controls checklist (POC level):
- KMS/HSM
  - Hosted: Confirm whether BYOK is available for POC or if tokenization/redaction is acceptable.
  - Dedicated: Request BYOK and verify SNK rotation policy.
  - Private: Customer-managed KMS/HSM; verify KMIP/HSM integration tests.
- Audit & Evidence
  - Ensure access to per-request audit logs; define retention. For hosted, capture logs via export to customer SIEM where feasible.
- Data residency
  - Hosted: Use region selection but verify backups & logs residency.
  - Dedicated/Private: Map VPC region to customer residency requirements.
- Network controls
  - Validate VPC peering or private link for dedicated/private paths. Confirm no public egress for sensitive flows.
- Tokenization and redaction layer
  - Implement local tokenization service that substitutes PII before sending to hosted instances if BYOK not available.
- Authentication & least privilege
  - Scoped API keys, short-lived credentials, and strict RBAC for all service accounts.

Recommended POC architecture (minimum viable zero-trust validation):
- Hybrid flow approach for POC (short timeline, low risk):
  1) Sensitive ingestion and tokenization live in-customer VPC (customer-managed service). Raw PII never leaves customer network. Tokenized payloads (non-reversible ID) sent to Redwood.
  2) Redwood Dedicated pool exposed via PrivateLink/VPC peering for tokenized workload. Dedicated chosen because it offers stronger network controls and predictable capacity without full private install overhead.
  3) Non-sensitive/low-risk batch workloads routed to hosted endpoints for cost efficiency and fast iteration.
  4) Audit logs for inference routed to a customer-owned log sink; if full per-request logs not available from hosted, log summaries and hashes are exchanged for reconciliation.

POC test plan (6-week cadence sample):
- Week 0: Kickoff, POAM, security questionnaire, define success metrics and sample dataset (masked).
- Week 1: Infrastructure setup: Dedicated pool reservation, VPC peering, KMS/BYOK feasibility check (or tokenization stub).
- Week 2: Integration: Tokenization service + Redwood SDK integration, create sample endpoints & traffic harness.
- Week 3: Security validation: penetration-lite (network scanning), key rotation test, logging verification.
- Week 4: Performance validation: Ramp to 30 TPS as defined, measure latency p50/p95/p99, measure token cost per request.
- Week 5: Failure modes & fallback: simulate Dedicated pool pressure and failover to hosted; verify rollback playbook and data quarantine.
- Week 6: Compliance runbook & deliverables: export logs, produce evidence pack, finalize recommendations and runbook.

Success criteria (POC completion):
- Sensitive-data path validated: no raw PII left customer VPC in 4-week test window.
- Latency targets met for 95th percentile under 30 TPS scenario.
- Audit logs available and consumable by customer SIEM for required retention window.
- Failover path validated within RTO (as defined with customer).

Estimated costs and resource needs (ballpark for POC):
- Infra: Dedicated reserve for 6 weeks (small pool): USD 6k–10k depending on GPU types.
- Engineering: 2 FTE-weeks (solutions + infra) + 1 SRE-week for peering and logging.
- Security testing: USD 1–2k for light pentest/scan tooling.
- Contingency: 20% buffer.

Potential blockers and mitigations:
- BYOK unavailable for short POC: mitigate with local tokenization and cryptographic binding (hash exchange) approach.
- Customer network change freezes: run hosted-sandbox path for non-sensitive work concurrently to avoid full block.
- Audit evidence gaps: pre-define what counts as evidence, include signed log digests and attestation.

Runbook snippets (operationally oriented):
- On incident (exposed token suspected):
  1) Quarantine traffic by toggling routing to hosted sandbox (non-sensitive) and pause Dedicated ingress.
  2) Rotate tokens/credentials for the tokenization bridge.
  3) Gather relevant logs (request hashes, timestamps) and escalate to security.
- Rollback: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% ramp back to hosted for low-risk flows. Sensitive flows should always be pinned to Dedicated/Private until post-POC handoff.

Deliverables for customer at close of POC:
- Short executive summary with recommendation and readiness level.
- Evidence pack: audit logs, KMS/HSM test results, network diagrams.
- Runbook: onboard/offboard steps, incident playbooks, key rotation steps.
- Cost model: short and long run projections for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Recommendation (for this customer's constraints and timeline):
- Execute a hybrid POC that uses a tokenization bridge + Redwood Dedicated pool for tokenized sensitive flows and Hosted endpoints for non-sensitive workloads. This balances security control, predictable performance, and time-to-results while keeping options open for a full Private deployment later if compliance requires BYOK/HSM under customer control.

Next actions (immediate):
1) Confirm customer acceptance of tokenization bridge pattern (response needed by +3 business days).
2) Create ENG ticket to reserve a small Dedicated pool and request VPC peering window.
3) Share POC plan and checklist with customer security team and schedule kickoff.

Notes and open questions to resolve with customer:
- Will the customer accept cryptographic hash-based evidence in lieu of full raw logs for the POC audit?
- Is there an internal timeline for migrating to customer-managed KMS (if required for production)?
- Who owns the tokenization bridge operationally after POC (customer vs Redwood-managed under contract)?

Appendix: quick-mark checklist for pre-kickoff
- Signed NDA and DPA in place.
- Customer SIEM log endpoint reachable and tested.
- Sample dataset (masked) delivered to solutions team.
- Network owners and security reviewers identified with contact points.

— end of note —
